notes: This is a BETA build - it is bug prone. If you encounter any bugs go to Help > Report Bug. Please stress test as much as you can!
Model generation was rewritten for this beta. Please try Make Model on as many items as you can, especially items with props and items with multiple models (timers, cube types, etc.)

added: Model generation no longer needs Java - VMF to OBJ conversion now runs inside BeePEE, so it's much faster and there's no Java download
Props in generated models now use their skin
Color tints now show in generated models (render color on props and brush entities, and material tints)
Models of other entities like turrets (npc_portal_turret_floor) are now included in generated models
Entities that get their model from the game (security cameras, buttons, chamber doors, cubes, ...) now show up in generated models
Overlays (info_overlay) like signage and indicator lights now show up in generated models, drawn into the textures of the faces they're on
Decals (infodecal) now show up in generated models
Displacements with blend materials now show both textures blended like in game
Adding or replacing an instance now tells you when it uses files that don't exist on your PC or aren't mounted properly (with what uses them), so you can fix them before players see missing textures

Icon maker: Make Icon in the item editor's Info tab generates the item's model and lets you line up the shot (3/4, front, side and top views, rotate, move, zoom, lens, shadow) to make its palette icon on the editor icons' grayish white background
fixed: Props (prop_static, prop_dynamic, ...) facing the wrong way in generated models
Animated props like item droppers showing in their raw pose instead of their default animation
Brush entities (func_detail etc.) ending up in the wrong place in items with multiple models
Brush textures being mirrored in generated models
Some brush faces missing from generated models
Make Model saying it completed when the generated model was empty - it now shows an error explaining why
Content in Portal 2/bee2 not being found during model generation
Transparent textures (glass, grates) showing up solid in generated models
Props sometimes getting another model's shape, or going missing, when a model couldn't be decompiled
Make Model failing on very big models (more than 65,535 vertices) when making the collision model
The item editor saying an item was saved when part of the save failed (like adding an instance or saving the conditions) - it now shows what failed and keeps your unsaved changes
Autopacking reporting an instance's materials and scripts as not packed when they were
Autopacking leaving out an instance's sounds, VScripts, model animations (.ani) and the textures of its materials when they're named differently than the material
Autopacking leaving out custom files put straight into Portal 2/portal2
Replacing an instance not packing the custom files the new one uses
Signage designer: Export as PNG and the signage's icon ignoring the texture resolution setting (they were always 512x512)
changed: Items with multiple models convert each instance on its own instead of merging them into one map
Normal maps are no longer copied into item materials (editor models don't use them)
Missing textures show as a purple/black checkerboard instead of the faces being left out
A prop's render color now only colors models made to be recolored (like BEE2's color cubes); other models keep their look
New cartoon style for generated models, closer to the editor's own models: flat clean colors, light greys and vivid accents
The cartoon style now runs inside BeePEE, so it's much faster and BeePEE no longer ships the Python cartoonify runtime
BeePEE no longer needs Python at all: finding a model's materials (autopacking, instance checks) and making collision models now run inside BeePEE, and finding materials is about 100x faster
Cleaner logs: plain text without emojis, with longer tasks like Make Model or loading a package shown as a tree of their steps and how long each took
The logs now also include what happens in BeePEE's windows (item editor, VBSP conditions, signage designer, ...), so bug reports show the whole picture
Log files stay small: chatty and repeated lines were cut, a log file is capped at 5 MB and only the 10 newest are kept

Autopacking tells the original game's files apart from custom ones by looking inside the game's VPKs: the base game and the official DLCs are never packed, neither are BEE2's files, and files an instance uses that don't exist anywhere are reported in the log
